why.text: Sunny south-Alpine valleys with big day-night swings, vineyards from 220 to over 1,000 m, varied soils and a very wide range of grapes.

styles.text: Mostly dry still whites and reds, often single-grape; also bottle-fermented sparkling, rosé, and sweet passito and late-harvest wines.

climate.text: Continental, on the sunny south side of the Alps. Mean temperatures run 9.5 to 13 °C with 1,800 to 2,300 sun hours a year. Rain is 450 to 600 mm in the north and about 860 mm in the far south. Day-night swings average up to 15 °C, peaking at 20 °C in September and October.

soil.text: Valley floors are fertile alluvial. Hill vineyards are mostly glacial moraine gravel. Between Merano and Bolzano the soil is often quartz porphyry; in the north quartz and mica; in the south limy soil from dolomite. About 60% of soils are light, sandy to gravelly.

altitude.text: Vineyards run from 220 to over 1,000 m: 29% at 220 to 300 m, 57% at 300 to 500 m, 14% above 500 m. Only 15% is flat; 30% is steep, over 30% slope.

tastes.text: Strong primary aromas: elderflower in Sauvignon, rose in Traminer, wild berries in Pinot Nero and Lagrein, cherry and violet in Schiava. High-altitude whites are fresh; lower reds are full with soft tannins.

styles.name: Riserva
styles.text: Aged at least two years from 1 October of harvest year; min 11.5% natural alcohol.

styles.name: Passito
styles.text: Semi-dried grapes, min 16% alcohol, max 40 hl/ha, sold from 1 June after harvest.

styles.name: Vendemmia tardiva
styles.text: Partly raisined on the vine, at least 13.5% natural alcohol, max 50 hl/ha.

styles.name: Spumante
styles.text: Bottle-fermented (metodo classico), at least 15 months in bottle.

why.text: Limestone-rich mountain valley slopes at 70 to 700 m, with cold snowy winters, warm summers and the Òra breeze from Lake Garda.

styles.text: Dry reds, whites and rosé, mostly single-grape; also sweet dried-grape Vino Santo and fortified Moscato.

climate.text: Fairly cold, snowy winters and warm, often muggy summers. Lake Garda gives the Alto Garda a milder, sub-Mediterranean climate. Mean annual temperatures run 11 to 13 °C; rain there is 900 to 1,000 mm.

soil.text: Mostly stony limestone debris with good drainage. Also porphyry in Valle di Cembra, basalt in central Vallagarina, and mica schist in Valsugana.

altitude.text: Vineyards for this DOC lie between 70 and 600/700 m above sea level.

tastes.text: Whites: straw yellow, dry, fruity or lightly aromatic, often fresh. Trentino rosso: deep ruby, dry, full, slightly tannic. Rosato: fresh, soft. Moscato giallo: aromatic, sometimes sweet. Moscato rosa: sweet, spiced nose.

styles.name: Vino Santo
styles.text: Nosiola dried on racks, pressed from 1 February, sold from third year after harvest.

styles.name: Riserva
styles.text: Aged at least one year for whites, two years for reds.

styles.name: Kretzer
styles.text: Rosé blend of at least two of Enantio, Schiava, Teroldego, Lagrein.

styles.name: Vendemmia tardiva
styles.text: Grapes partly dried on the vine for a longer or shorter time.

why.text: Hills of marl and sandstone flysch, sheltered from cold north winds by the Julian Prealps and warmed by sunlight reflected from the nearby Adriatic.

styles.text: Mostly dry varietal and blended whites, plus reds; Picolit is off-dry to sweet.

climate.text: Hot but not muggy summers and cold, fairly rainy winters; mean summer 21.5 to 22.5 °C, winter about 4 °C, rainfall 1350 to 1400 mm a year.

soil.text: Flysch of marl and sandstone from Eocene and Paleocene seabeds, with marine fossils; well drained, rooting depth on average 50 to 100 cm, sometimes 150 cm.

altitude.text: Vineyards on hills averaging 60 to 270 m, slopes on average 15 to 30%; valley floor and plain sites are excluded, bar reshaped hillside plots and zone-one foothills above 85 m.

tastes.text: Bianco: straw to deep gold, delicate, lightly aromatic, dry, fresh, harmonious. Rosso: ruby, slightly herbaceous, dry, full-bodied. Picolit: off-dry or sweet, warm.

styles.name: Riserva
styles.text: Red aged 30 months (at least 6 in wood), white 20 months; no enrichment.

styles.name: Picolit
styles.text: Off-dry or sweet white; maximum 4 t/ha, at least 14% total alcohol.

styles.name: Cabernet
styles.text: Name reserved for Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and/or Carmenere.

styles.name: Bianco
styles.text: Blend of authorised whites; Muller Thurgau and Traminer limited to 15% of the total.

why.text: Soft terraced hills of marl and sandstone, sheltered from cold northern winds by the Julian Prealps, with the nearby sea softening temperature swings.

styles.text: Dry white and red wines named by grape, plus Bianco, Rosso, sweet Dolce and a copper-pink Pinot grigio ramato.

climate.text: Julian Prealps shelter the hills from cold northern winds; the sea, no more than 40 km away, softens temperature swings. Mean annual temperature is about 15 °C, 18 to 19 °C from April to October, with 1800 to 1900 degree-days. Growing-season rain is about 1157 mm at Ramandolo, 976 mm at Cividale and under 900 mm in the south.

soil.text: Flysch di Cormòns, alternating marl and sandstone locally called ponca, of Eocene origin; marls hold 40 to 60% limestone. Damp valley-floor land is excluded.

altitude.text: Vineyards lie between 100 and 400 m, mostly on terraced hills; the soft marl hills are mostly well below 200 m.

tastes.text: Whites: fine, elegant, fruity and floral, dry and lively. Reds: dry, full-bodied and harmonious. Dolce: sweet, intense, perhaps with a hint of wood.

styles.name: Riserva
styles.text: White or red aged at least two years from 1 November of the harvest year.

styles.name: Pignolo
styles.text: Riserva needs four years' ageing; sold no earlier than November of the third year after harvest.

styles.name: Pinot grigio ramato
styles.text: Copper-pink Pinot grigio made with light pre-fermentation skin contact, at least 85% Pinot grigio.

styles.name: Dolce
styles.text: Sweet wine from white grapes including Picolit, at least 12% alcohol.

why.text: Coarse, stony limestone-dolomite gravel from alpine rivers, sheltered from cold north winds and helped by the Adriatic, with big day-night swings.

styles.text: Varietal and blended whites and reds, plus rosato, novello, frizzante and spumante, from dry to sweet Verduzzo.

climate.text: Temperate sub-continental: mean annual temperature 10 to 14.4 °C, rain 1,100 to 2,000 mm a year, and warmer and drier from north to south.

soil.text: Alluvial gravel of limestone and dolomite, coarser in the north and finer in the south, with 20 to 60% stones. Wet or spring-fed land is excluded.

altitude.text: The high plain lies between 5 and 320 metres.

tastes.text: Whites: straw yellow, fine and dry to off-dry. Reds: ruby turning garnet with age, intense, sometimes herbal (Cabernet). Aromatic, elegant wines.

styles.name: Superiore
styles.text: Higher minimum alcohol (11.5%), and yields cut to 10 tonnes per hectare.

styles.name: Riserva
styles.text: Released two years after 11 November of the harvest year; not for novello or rosato.

styles.name: Spumante
styles.text: From Chardonnay, Pinot bianco or Pinot nero: extra brut, brut, extra dry, dry, demi-sec.

styles.name: Frizzante
styles.text: Lightly sparkling, bubbles from natural fermentation in a closed tank.

why.text: Terraced hills of Eocene marl and sandstone, sheltered from cold north winds by the Julian Prealps, with the sea near. Late-picked, partly dried Picolit.

styles.text: One golden, off-dry to sweet white from Picolit, often from dried grapes; the Cialla subzone may also be Riserva.

climate.text: Mean annual temperature about 15 °C, 18 to 19 °C from April to October. Prealps shelter from cold northern winds, and the sea is within 40 km. Growing-season rain is 1157 mm at Tarcento and Nimis, about 976 mm at Cividale, under 900 mm in the south.

soil.text: Flysch of Cormòns: alternating marl (40 to 60% limestone) and sandstone, called ponca, of Eocene origin. Erodible, so hills are terraced. Valley floors are excluded.

altitude.text: Vineyards lie between 100 and 400 m, mostly on terraced hills; the soft hills stay well below 200 m.

tastes.text: Golden yellow. Intense nose, sometimes like passito wine, fine, with a possible slight hint of wood. Off-dry to sweet, warm and harmonious.

styles.name: Cialla
styles.text: Subzone in Prepotto: 100% Picolit, 14% minimum natural alcohol, Riserva allowed.

why.text: Steep, terraced marl hills sheltered by Monte Bernadia, with high rainfall and big temperature swings before harvest, give a late-picked, partly dried Verduzzo.

styles.text: Golden sweet white from 100% Verduzzo Friulano (verduzzo giallo), also as Riserva.

climate.text: Rainfall above 2,200 mm a year, with about 130 rainy days. Mean temperature is 13.6 °C, summer peaks above 30 °C and in winter it is not rare to drop below zero. Monte Bernadia shields the vines from cold north winds.

soil.text: Mostly Eocene marl (the Flysch of Cormons, called ponca), with limestone landslide debris from Monte Bernadia. Slopes can exceed 30%.

altitude.text: Vineyards lie from 250 m at Torlano to 369 m at Ramandolo, up to 413 m at Sedilis, all facing south.

tastes.text: Golden, intense, sweet and velvety, lightly tannic and full-bodied. Notes of acacia, ripe plum, apricot and mountain honey. Riserva may add citrus, candied fruit, green tea, saffron.

styles.name: Ramandolo
styles.text: 100% Verduzzo Friulano, minimum 14% total alcohol, sold from November of the year after harvest.

styles.name: Ramandolo Riserva
styles.text: Sold no earlier than 1 December of the third year after harvest.

why.text: Hills of crumbly marl and sandstone flysch, milder and drier than the rest of the province, planted to Friulano-led white blends.

others: Other white grapes suitable for Udine province (up to 5% in total)

styles.text: Only one style: a dry white wine.

climate.text: Growing-season mean temperature is 18.6 °C and rainfall 915 mm; the annual mean is 14.2 °C with 1290 mm of rain. It is milder and drier than the provincial average, being closer to the sea and farther from the mountains.

soil.text: Mostly Eocene marl and sandstone known as flysch (local name ponca), with marl prevailing. It is crumbly, silty clay loam and moderately alkaline, and needs terracing and drainage against erosion.

tastes.text: Dry, harmonious and winey, with a delicate scent and balanced acidity. Rich, silky, refined and elegant, with long ageing in the best years.
